\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{index::doc}}


\sphinxAtStartPar
PlussMic is the data\sphinxhyphen{}analysis layer in the Pluss stack. It gives you three related models:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Atlas}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kindle}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Stream}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Catalog}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Archive}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bundle}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Slot}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Registry}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Aisle}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This manual is organized the same way users usually approach the library:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
start with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}} for table\sphinxhyphen{}style analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Thread}} when you want typed column operations outside a frame

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Catalog}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Archive}} when streams/case\sphinxhyphen{}aligned data are a better fit

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Registry}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Aisle}} when you want heterogeneous record bundles

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope

\chapter{DataFrame Guide}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe:dataframe-guide}}\label{\detokenize{dataframe::doc}}

\section{What DataFrame Is Good At}
\label{\detokenize{dataframe:what-dataframe-is-good-at}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::table::DataFrame}} is the main table\sphinxhyphen{}analysis surface in PlussMic.
Use it when you want:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
named features with mixed typed columns

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a case axis that can be numeric, note\sphinxhyphen{}based, timeline\sphinxhyphen{}based, or time\sphinxhyphen{}index based

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
table verbs such as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{assign}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{group\_by}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pivot\_table}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{join}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fillna}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{describe}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
import/export across CSV, TXT, JSON, Excel, and Parquet

\end{itemize}

\section{When To Use Kindle Types}
\label{\detokenize{kindle:when-to-use-kindle-types}}

The kindle model is stream\sphinxhyphen{}first:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Stream}}: one typed vector plus optional validity mask and case labels

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Catalog}}: named collection of streams

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Archive}}: depth stack of catalogs

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the right model when case alignment and stream\sphinxhyphen{}native transforms matter more than table presentation.

\section{When To Use Bundle Types}
\label{\detokenize{bundle:when-to-use-bundle-types}}

The bundle model is the heterogeneous record layer:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Slot}}: sequence of heterogeneous Pluss values

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Registry}}: named set of slots

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Aisle}}: depth stack of registries

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use it when one field can hold different domain types, or when you want a lighter record/batch abstraction than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DataFrame}}.
